text: Write a program that computes ten dimes two ways and shows which is right. Fill in the three blanks.
choices: for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++) { ___; ___; }   // add a dime each way
System.out.println("integer cents : " + ___);  // convert for display only
explanation: Verified: 1.0 from the integer path and 0.9999999999999999 from the double path. Ten dimes is a dollar, and one of these two programs disagrees. Note where the division sits: the integers accumulate exactly and are converted to a decimal fraction only at the moment of display, which is the general pattern — compute in the exact representation and convert at the boundary, never the reverse.
